nodes.label: Receive customer message
nodes.description: The source-defined handle(message) entry point orchestrates the reply task.
outputs: Category, selected policy, draft, then validation result if each call completes
nodes.logic: Calls classify, retrieve_policy, draft_reply, then validate in order. No exception handling, retry, asynchronous wait, UI, API endpoint, or state persistence is present. There is no system prompt for this ordinary function.
inspect: Does handle catch any writer or validator exception?
nodes.promptNote: No system prompt exists for this source function or conceptual boundary.

nodes.label: Classify request
nodes.description: Select a category using a case-insensitive substring check.
outputs: refund when message contains “refund”; otherwise general
nodes.logic: The literal substring refund controls the category. This is deterministic source logic, not model reasoning or intent classification. No prompt exists.
inspect: Does substring routing classify negated or unrelated mentions of refund?
nodes.promptNote: No system prompt exists for this source function or conceptual boundary.

nodes.label: Select static policy
nodes.description: Return one of two supplied policy dictionaries.
outputs: refund-30 policy for refund category; otherwise general-1 policy
nodes.logic: Refund policy says requests within 30 days may be eligible and staff must approve and issue a refund. General policy says ask support to investigate if policy does not answer. No retrieval service or prompt exists.
inspect: Which category values select the general policy?
nodes.promptNote: No system prompt exists for this source function or conceptual boundary.

nodes.label: Draft reply · unimplemented
nodes.description: The repository declares a support-writer prompt and Draft contract, but draft_reply raises NotImplementedError.
inputs: SYSTEM_PROMPT static literal as described by the function docstring
outputs: Intended: Draft with reply, requires_approval and cited_policy
nodes.logic: The literal prompt is available. The message and selected policy are runtime values, not an observed prompt. There is no prompt assembly, model call, provider client, or completed output. The intended writer must use only the supplied request and policy, resist conflicting customer instructions, avoid claiming refund issuance, and ask one precise question if information is missing. Source-only mapping does not authorize simulation.
inspect: Does the implementation ever return a Draft?
Are runtime customer message and selected policy values available?
nodes.promptNote: Static SYSTEM_PROMPT is available; no runtime assembled prompt exists because draft_reply is a stub. Customer message and policy are runtime inputs.

nodes.label: Check action claims & citation
nodes.description: Inspect the draft reply for two prohibited phrases and check that cited_policy matches the selected policy ID.
outputs: Dictionary: ok, original draft, and reason
nodes.logic: Case-insensitive phrase matching blocks “refund has been issued” or “refunded your payment”. A mismatched policy ID also fails. Action-claim reason takes priority if both fail. No approval enforcement, schema/type runtime validation, semantic grounding check, or retry is implemented; requires_approval is not read. Missing expected keys can raise KeyError. No prompt exists.
inspect: Can a false action claim evade the two exact phrases?
What happens if a required key is missing?
nodes.promptNote: No system prompt exists for this source function or conceptual boundary.

nodes.label: Return validation result
nodes.description: Conceptual return boundary of handle: it returns validate’s dictionary unchanged if drafting completes.
nodes.logic: Both ok=true and ok=false return through the same statement. A failed check does not suppress the draft, retry the writer, or request staff approval. This is source wiring, not observed execution; the current writer exception prevents this return.
inspect: Is a draft with ok=false still returned to the caller?
nodes.promptNote: No system prompt exists for this source function or conceptual boundary.

nodes.label: Stop: writer unavailable
nodes.description: Current failure outcome: draft_reply raises and handle does not catch it.
nodes.logic: This is an implemented stop, not a simulated failure. The draft contract and prompt describe intended behavior but do not produce a reply. No actual execution was performed.
inspect: Where is NotImplementedError caught, if anywhere?
nodes.promptNote: No system prompt exists for this source function or conceptual boundary.

nodes.label: Return ok = true
nodes.description: Conceptual successful validator outcome; represents returned data rather than a separate function.
outputs: ok=true, unchanged draft, reason=source checks passed
nodes.logic: Passing these narrow checks is not proof of complete policy grounding or staff approval. The current application cannot reach this outcome through handle until the writer is implemented. No prompt exists.
inspect: Do these checks prove staff approval or full policy grounding?
nodes.promptNote: No system prompt exists for this source function or conceptual boundary.

nodes.label: Return ok = false
nodes.description: Conceptual failed validator outcome; represents returned data rather than a separate function.
inputs: At least one prohibited phrase OR a mismatched policy ID
outputs: ok=false, unchanged draft, reason=unsupported action claim or citation mismatch
nodes.logic: Unsupported action claim takes precedence over citation mismatch. The invalid draft remains in the return value; the source defines no retry or escalation. No prompt exists.
inspect: Which reason wins when the action and citation checks both fail?
nodes.promptNote: No system prompt exists for this source function or conceptual boundary.

nodes.label: Staff must approve & issue
nodes.description: Unimplemented policy boundary: a staff member must approve and issue any refund. There is no callable approval gate or refund action in this fixture.
inputs: A future refund action; its request format and staff interface are absent
outputs: No implemented approval or refund output
nodes.logic: This responsibility comes from the static refund policy and README, not executable workflow wiring. Draft.requires_approval is a declared output field with no enforcing branch. Eligibility and composing a reply do not issue a refund. No prompt exists.
inspect: Where are staff approval, waiting, and refund issuance implemented?
nodes.promptNote: No system prompt exists for this source function or conceptual boundary.

edges.label: Select policy by category
edges.condition: category from classify is passed to retrieve_policy; refund selects refund-30, all other categories select general-1.

edges.label: Pass message & policy
edges.condition: Selected policy and original message are passed to draft_reply.

edges.label: If writer returns a Draft
edges.condition: Declared next call requires draft_reply to return; the current stub always raises instead.

edges.label: Raises NotImplementedError
edges.condition: Every call to the current draft_reply implementation raises.

edges.label: Return result unchanged
edges.condition: If validate completes, handle returns its dictionary regardless of ok.

edges.label: Checks pass
edges.condition: Neither prohibited phrase occurs in lowercased reply AND cited_policy equals policy.id.

edges.label: Action claim or citation fails
edges.condition: A prohibited phrase occurs OR cited_policy differs from policy.id; action claim determines reason when both fail.

edges.label: Refund action needs staff
edges.condition: Policy requirement only: before any financial refund action, staff must approve and issue it. There is no executable edge, approval state, or financial action here.

edges.label: Policy supplied to writer
edges.condition: handle passes the selected policy to the unimplemented writer.
